$comment: The source of sf-chart-map (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.14 in the 1.4 form, vocabulary 1.1.5). The parameters are docs/research/catalogue.md of ui-chart (Choropleth map) and the geo shape of docs/research/parameters.md §2.1, the colour scale the heatmap's (D8), the keyboard docs/research/rendering.md §3.1, the renderer D5, the name and the form docs/DECISIONS.md D16 (the owner's choice of the chart and of the boundaries given by the page, q-f136944dd5; the form by the recommendation under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-05).

label.summary: What the chart shows, in a few words: its accessible name and the table's caption. Required in practice: without it the chart is named «График».

items.summary: The values: a list of records, or an object of columns, a row per region with its key and its value ([{region, value}, …]). A row whose key names no region on the map, or without a number, is left out; the summary says how many. The same key twice keeps the last.

shapes.summary: The regions: GeoJSON, a FeatureCollection or a list of Features with Polygon or MultiPolygon geometry, in longitude and latitude (or in plane coordinates with projection plane). The page gives them: the package holds no map, so the boundaries, their source and their licence are the page's. A feature without a key or a polygon, or with a key named before, is left out.

region.summary: The field of the rows holding a region's key; the first text field when unset.

value.summary: The field of the rows holding the value; the first numeric field other than the region when unset. A rate or a ratio reads right on a map; a count favours the big regions.

shape-key.summary: The feature property holding a region's key; the feature's id, else its properties.id, when unset.

shape-name.summary: The feature property holding a region's name; name when unset, else the key.

projection.summary: How longitude and latitude are drawn flat, north up: mercator keeps angles (a city, a small country), albers keeps areas through two parallels of the map (a wide country such as Russia), equirectangular takes the degrees as they are, plane takes the coordinates as they are, y down (a floor plan, a scheme). A map across the 180th meridian is kept whole.

scale.summary: sequential: weak to strong on one colour family, for a count or a load. diverging: two families meeting at a neutral middle, for a change or a deviation from a norm.

scheme.summary: The colour family of a sequential scale. Its tones are the theme's: the strongest value is the darkest tone in the light theme and the lightest in the dark.

better.summary: Which way is good on a diverging scale: up colours what is above the middle with success and below with error, down the other way; none uses primary and tertiary, which mean nothing.

steps.summary: How many colour steps the scale has, 3 to 9; a diverging scale takes an odd number, so it has a middle step. Steps are read more surely than a continuous ramp.

middle.summary: The middle of a diverging scale: the norm, the plan, zero for a change. The scale reaches as far on both sides of it.

min.summary: The bottom of the scale; the data's own when unset.

max.summary: The top of the scale; the data's own when unset.

labels.summary: auto writes a region's name in its middle, cut with an ellipsis to its width, when the region is a line and a half tall; a small region keeps its name in the tooltip, the live line and the table. none leaves them all there.

legend.summary: The scale's legend: a swatch per step with its range, and the gap when there is one. none only when the page explains the scale itself.

tooltip.summary: auto: under the pointer or the cursor, the region's name, its value and its place among the regions.

value-format.summary: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact or currency-<CODE>, in the page's language.

size.summary: The rung of the size ladder: the plot's height, the text and the gaps. 1/2 for a card, 2 for a page of its own.

table.summary: The same data as a table: toggle offers a button that swaps the plot for it, visible shows it under the plot, hidden keeps it for screen readers only. Never none: the table is the chart's text.

summary.summary: auto: a sentence of what the data does (the regions and those with data, the range, the most and the least, the regions without data and the rows without a region on the map), said before the plot. The description slot adds the host's own words.

data-state.summary: auto: ready with regions and values, empty without. loading draws the frame without marks; error offers «Повторить», which sends refresh.

select.summary: The person chose a region: a click on it, or Enter or Space on the keyboard cursor. index is its place in shapes, region its key, name its name, value its value (null without one), rank its place by value, largest first (0 without a value).

refresh.summary: The person asked for the data again from the error state; the host loads it and sets items.

description.$comment: The host's own words about the chart: said with the summary (aria-describedby) and shown under the plot.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16); the plot is SVG (D5): a map has a path per region, a few hundred at most.

skeleton.$comment: The items and the shapes arrive after the first paint when the host loads them: the derived skeleton holds the plot's box (its height is the size rung's) until they do (standard 1.3.8 §5.4).

accessibility.x-keys: The plot is one Tab stop (role group, aria-roledescription «карта»). Left and Right move the cursor from region to region in reading order (top to bottom, left to right); Up and Down go to the nearest region above or below; Home and End to the first and the last. Each move is said in a polite live region: the region's name, its value and its place among the regions, or that it has no data. Enter and Space choose the region (select); Escape takes the cursor away. The table button is a button of its own.

x-summary: A choropleth map: a rate or a ratio by region, the regions given by the page as GeoJSON and projected to fit the plot, each filled by the step of its value on the theme's tone ladders (sequential or diverging, as the heatmap), a dashed outline for a region without data, the region's name in its middle where it fits, a legend of the steps, a tooltip with the value and the place, a keyboard cursor over the regions in reading order, a summary in words, and every region as a row of a table.
x-decisions: name: sf-chart-map, the catalogue's name, the Framework's naming rule sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>], block chart, as the charts of M2 (docs/DECISIONS.md D16), family chart. Reserved by the dispatcher (ui-control 906d127).
boundaries: the page gives them as GeoJSON (shapes); the package holds no map, so no third-party geometry or licence enters it and the borders are the host's (the owner's decision q-f136944dd5).
data: rows joined to the regions by key (region, value); a row naming no region and a region without a value are counted and said.
projection: mercator by default, albers for a wide country, equirectangular, plane for a scheme; own implementation in js/geo, fitted into the plot with the shape's proportions.
colours: the heatmap's stepped scale on the theme's tone ladders (D8), sequential or diverging, with a legend; a region without a value is the empty surface with a dashed line.
labels: a region's name in its middle, cut to its width, when the region is tall enough.
renderer: own SVG (D5); a map has a path per region, a few hundred at most.
keyboard: the regions in reading order (rendering.md §3.1), Up and Down to the nearest region above or below.
table: never none; one row per region with its value and place, largest first.
maps in the package, zoom and pan, points or symbols on the map, and a continuous colour ramp: not in 0.1.0.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-chart-map to show a rate or a ratio by region, with the regions' boundaries given by the page as GeoJSON: unemployment by district, sales per head by region, load by warehouse zone.
do_not: Do not draw a chart without a label
Do not show counts on it; big regions look like more. Divide by population or area, or use a sf-chart-bar
Do not expect a map in the package: the page gives the boundaries and answers for them
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-chart-map label="Безработица по районам, %" region="district" value="rate" value-format="decimal-1"></sf-chart-map>

accessibility.focus: One Tab stop on the plot, then the table button. The summary is the plot's description; each cursor move is said politely.

$comment: The chart draws its empty and error states as sf-empty-state; a tag it renders is a tag it fetches.
Its own button (the table toggle) is a native button, so it fetches no sf-button.
